messages.subject: hyper > prior > prior
parts:
I have a model where I estimate 2 equations at the same time. I use a Gamma prior for parameter theta. 

I want theta1 in eq 1 to influence theta2 in eq 2. I could do

theta1 ~ gamma(2, 1)
theta2 ~ gamma(theta1, 1)

because a/b is the mean of a Gamma distribution.

But I feel it might not be elegant, as I might mis-set the variance of theta2. What's a better way?

--

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] hyper > prior > prior
parts:
Unless there's more than one observation for theta2, you won't
be able to estimate theta1 anyway, and if there is more than one
observation, you can estimate the second parameter of the gamma.

- Bob
